title: Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency: Long-Term Care Insurer Share in a Resumption Deposit
content:
**Insurance assignment desk Q&A — Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency.** These answers concern the resumption insurer share, taken off the daily rate of the resumption deposit where a long-term care insurer pays on the agreement under an assignment of benefits. "Within the last three months" counts payments dated fewer than three whole calendar months before the day the resumption deposit is worked out.

**The insurer paid on the agreement at least three times within the last three months.** The share is the insurer's most recent payment on the agreement (the one posted first where two share a date) divided by the days of the charge that payment paid; nothing where that charge shows no days.

**The insurer paid within the last three months, but fewer than three times.** The share is the insurer's payments on the agreement within the last three months divided by 91, the averaging days.

**The insurer has not paid within the last three months.** No insurer share is taken off.

**Hypothetical cases.** Five payments in the window, the latest 1,240.00 against a 31-day charge: 40.00 a day. One payment of 455.00: 455.00 divided by 91 is 5.00 a day.
